terms.meaning: a fixed value that does not change while the app runs

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Limit and imports
sections.what: Brings in the project type and sets the maximum of 100,000 activities for a full model.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps full models within a size the browser can handle.
sections.watch_out: Other code may keep its own copy of this number, so a change here may not apply everywhere.

sections.name: requiresDirectProgramme
sections.title: Single large project check
sections.what: Returns true only when exactly one project has more activities than the limit.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single very large project should use the paged view, while smaller groups stay on the full model.
sections.watch_out: Two large projects together return false, so their combined size is not limited by this check.

summary: Decides whether a single project is so large that the app should show it in the paged programme view. This happens only when exactly one project is given and it has more than 100,000 activities.
purpose: Keeps very large single projects from loading all at once.
why: Likely reason: a model with too many activities would be too heavy to render in the browser. The reason for the 100,000 figure is not stated in the code.
how: Stores the limit as a fixed constant. The check returns true only when there is exactly one project and its activity count is above the limit. A missing count counts as zero.
inputs: A list of project references, each with an activity count.
risks: Several large projects together still use the full model, so their combined size is not limited. The limit must match any limit the backend applies.
debug: If a large project does not go to the paged view, check that exactly one project was passed and that its count is present.
